verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. It shares the 'communication complexity rank' vocabulary but does not interact with the specific claim about Brauer group order bounds.

verdicts.title: Schur multipliers of special p-groups of rank 2
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A group G is called special p-group of rank k if the commutator subgroup [G,G] and centre Z(G) are equal, which is elementary abelian p-group of rank k and G/[G,G] is also elementary abelian p-group. In this article we determine the Schur multiplier of special p-groups of rank 2 explicitly.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses Schur multipliers of special p-groups of rank 2, a pure group theory topic, with no mention of Brauer groups, Boolean functions, or communication complexity rank as in the conjecture.
